title: TCP and UDP
subtitle: IP delivers packets when it feels like it. TCP turns that into a reliable, ordered stream — and learns how fast it may go.

ports.title: Process-to-process delivery
ports.body: The network layer gets a packet to a host; the transport layer gets it to a process. A 16-bit port number identifies the process; the pair (IP, port) is a socket. The sender multiplexes many applications onto one network connection; the receiver demultiplexes by port. UDP adds only ports and a checksum: fast, connectionless, no guarantees (DNS, streaming, games). TCP adds connections, reliability, ordering, flow and congestion control (web, email, files).

hs.title: The three-way handshake
hs.body: Before data flows TCP agrees initial sequence numbers: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, the client ACKs. Teardown uses FIN and ACK in each direction (a four-step close), since each side closes its half independently. Press Simulate to watch the segments cross.

reliable.title: Reliability and flow control
reliable.body: TCP numbers every byte. The receiver's acknowledgement is cumulative ("I have everything up to byte N"). Loss is detected by a timeout or by three duplicate ACKs (fast retransmit). The receiver also advertises a window, the free space in its buffer, and the sender never has more than that outstanding: flow control stops a fast sender overrunning a slow receiver. It is the sliding window of the previous chapter, applied to a byte stream.
reliable.steps: A receiver advertises a 4000-byte window; the sender has sent bytes 1000–2999 unacknowledged. It may send 4000 − 2000 = 2000 more bytes.

cc.title: Congestion control
cc.body: Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects the network. TCP keeps a congestion window cwnd. Slow start: cwnd doubles each RTT from 1 until it reaches ssthresh. Congestion avoidance: +1 segment per RTT. On three duplicate ACKs, Reno halves the threshold and continues from there (fast recovery); Tahoe restarts from 1. A timeout sends both back to 1. The saw-tooth is the signature of TCP.

sockets.title: Sockets
sockets.body: A socket is the programmer’s handle on this machinery. A server calls socket → bind → listen → accept and then recv/send; a client calls socket → connect then send/recv. accept returns a new socket for each client while the listening socket keeps waiting.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Ports pick processes; TCP = reliable stream, UDP = datagrams.
  • Handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.
  • Flow control = receiver’s window; congestion control = cwnd (slow start, AIMD).
